description:
Hey everyone! 🚀 We’re a Stuttgart-based team looking for teammates—both for this hackathon and for future long-term projects! All skill sets are welcome.

This time around, we’re creating a web-based lunar base simulator game where players step into the shoes of an astronaut on the Moon. We're actively looking for web designers, developers, pitch presenters, and anyone else excited about the concept.

Drop us a line, tell us a bit about yourself, and we'll reply right away!
summary: An interactive 3D Digital Twin and resource-management simulator for lunar and Martian habitats. By integrating high-detail 3D architectural modules with real-time physical constraints (mass, power generation, oxygen regeneration, and thermal load), our web platform allows mission planners to test base configurations and prevent critical system failures before deployment.
details:
How It Works & Use of NASA Data

Users configure an extraterrestrial outpost by selecting modular components—including habitats, solar arrays, life-support units, and rovers—within strict launch payload mass and budget caps. The simulation engine calculates resource equilibrium across extreme environmental cycles, incorporating open NASA reference parameters:

Lunar Day/Night Cycle: Accounting for the 14-Earth-day lunar night energy storage bottleneck based on NASA Artemis surface mission architectures.

Life Support (ECLSS): Oxygen consumption and power-draw baselines modeled after International Space Station (ISS) Environmental Control and Life Support System data.

Payload Constraints: Launch mass limits aligned with heavy-lift lunar lander specifications.

Tech Stack & Architecture

3D Modeling & Rendering: Custom isometric engineering assets modeled and rendered in Blender.

Simulation Core & Frontend: Built in Python using Streamlit for real-time telemetry dashboards and interactive parameter control, accelerated through AI-assisted architectural prototyping.

Impact & Future Scalability

Beyond serving as an accessible educational and rapid-prototyping tool for space mission architecture, this Digital Twin framework is built for dual-use scalability. The underlying closed-loop resource algorithm can be adapted directly to Earth-based extreme environments, such as vertical farming facilities (AgTech), off-grid research stations, and microgrid energy management.
dataRefs: Crew metabolic mass-balance baselines for pressurized lunar habitats — nominal metabolic $\\text{O}_2$ consumption ($0.84\\text{ kg/person/day}$), $\\text{CO}_2$ output ($1.00\\text{ kg/person/day}$), and potable/hygiene water baseline ($2.5\\text{ kg/person/day}$).
Closed-loop water recovery efficiency ($93\\%\\text{–}98\\%$), oxygen generation via water electrolysis and Sabatier $\\text{CO}_2$ reduction, and active thermal radiator rejection loads.

Lunar South Pole (Shackleton Crater rim) solar illumination profile ($\\sim 86\\%$ continuous sunlight availability), permanently shadowed region (PSR) water-ice prospecting constraints for ISRU, and diurnal lunar surface thermal swing parameters.
Trans-lunar injection (TLI) and landed surface payload mass constraints ($50.0\\text{ metric tons}$ mission mass budget).
